cards.text: The Pharisees and some of the scribes who had come from Jerusalem gather around Jesus. The Pharisees are a strict group of Jewish religious leaders, and the scribes are teachers of the law. They see some of His disciples eating with hands that were defiled, that is, unwashed.

cards.question: The Gospel of Mark explains that some people don't eat until they wash their hands ceremonially, holding to the tradition of the elders. Who does this?

answers.text: The Pharisees and all the Jews
Only the priests at the temple

cards.question: When the Pharisees and all the Jews come back from the market, they eat without washing first. True or false?

cards.text: And they have many other traditions, like washing cups, pitchers, kettles and even couches for dining. They wash the COUCHES, friend, and I sat in a junk drawer for years without anybody dusting me ONCE.

cards.question: So the Pharisees and scribes question Jesus about His disciples. What do they want to know?

answers.text: Why they skip the elders' tradition
Why they work on the Sabbath
Why they don't fast like others

cards.text: Jesus answers them, “Isaiah prophesied correctly about you hypocrites…” and then He quotes Isaiah, a prophet (Isaiah 29:13). Oof.

cards.question: In the words Jesus quotes from Isaiah, these people honor God with their lips. True or false?
In the words Jesus quotes, these people's hearts are far from God, and they worship Him in vain. What do they teach as doctrine?
Then Jesus says it plainly to the Pharisees and scribes: they've disregarded the ___ of God to keep the tradition of men.

cards.text: He goes on, “You neatly set aside the command of God to maintain your own tradition.” Neatly, friend. Like folding a fresh apron.
Then Jesus gives an example, quoting Moses, Israel's leader (Exodus 20:12; 21:17): “Honor your father and your mother” and “Anyone who curses his father or mother must be put to death.”
But here's their tradition: a man can tell his father or mother that whatever they would have received from him is Corban, a gift devoted to God.

cards.question: Jesus says that under their tradition, once a man calls it Corban, what is he permitted to do for his father or mother?

cards.text: Jesus says that by the tradition they've handed down, they nullify the word of God, and they do so in many such matters. Corban isn't one cookie, friend. It's a whole BATCH.
Once again Jesus calls the crowd to Him and says, “All of you, listen to Me and understand:” That's the kind of line that makes a whole room put their phones face-down.

cards.question: Jesus tells the crowd that something can't defile a man at all. What is it?

answers.text: Anything that enters him from outside
Anything he says when he's angry

cards.question: Jesus tells the crowd it's the things that come out of a man that defile him. True or false?

cards.text: Later Jesus leaves the crowd and goes into the house, and His disciples ask Him about the parable.
Jesus asks them, “Are you still so dull?” Friend, I spent years in a drawer with worn-down edges, and let me tell you, dull is NOT a fun place to be.

cards.question: Jesus tells the disciples that what enters a man from the outside goes into his heart. True or false?

cards.text: It doesn't enter his heart, Jesus says. It goes into the stomach and then is eliminated.

cards.question: Right after Jesus' words, the Gospel of Mark adds a short note: thus all foods are ___.
Jesus tells the disciples that what comes out of a man is what defiles him. Where does it come from?

answers.text: From within the hearts of men

cards.text: Then Jesus lists what comes out: evil thoughts, sexual immorality, theft, murder, adultery, greed, wickedness, deceit, debauchery, envy, slander, arrogance and foolishness. All these evils come from within, Jesus says, and these are what defile a man.
